frontier.hypothesis: On K7's spine (the gp store AFTER the 0x1A store, which is the only spine measured to put the third load at slot 11 at 66 instructions), some statement placed between the +2 read and the 0x1A store is a $v0 donor whose own instructions belong where target puts them -- and that body is the match.
frontier.mechanism: L1 proves the donor's identity is free (a copy works, the gp store works); L4 proves the idx read does not donate; the copy donates but its lw/lw/sw triple lands at 21/23/26 instead of 16/18/20. What is needed is a donor whose emitted instructions are already scheduled in target's window slots 25-26, i.e. a two-instruction addiu/store pair -- of which the function has exactly two, D_800A3478 and D_800A347C, and both have been priced on the E2 spine but NOT as donors on K7's spine with every surrounding position swept.
frontier.next_probe: On the K7 spine, sweep the D_800A347C addiu/store pair through the window between the +2 read and the 0x1A store, crossed with all positions of P, S4 and S5 and all legal tails, extracting the QTYDBG got value for reg74 and the load slots for each body. Q1-Q8 measured S7 early on the E2/copy spines only (68 insns); it has never been measured as the window donor on the spine that already has the slot-11 load.

frontier.hypothesis: N2's 65-instruction body closes if p10's load can be held out of the slot-4 load-delay slot while its read still precedes the copy block.
frontier.mechanism: N2 is target's stream shifted one slot earlier because the load fills a nop target keeps. The load is ready because it depends only on $v1. Anything that makes the load's operand not yet available at that point -- or that gives sched2 a higher-ranked insn for slot 4 -- restores the nop and re-emits the load at 11.
frontier.next_probe: On the N2 spine, sweep statements into the gap between `outer = D_800A3468;` and the p10 read, and sweep the zero store's own position, watching whether slot 4 is a nop and whether the load re-emerges at 11. Also extract the sched2 trace (tools/grinder/dump.ps1 then the .sched2 dump) for N2 at T-61..T-57 to name the rank_for_schedule comparison that put the load there.

frontier.hypothesis: The disposition entries filed 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-01 rest on a premise that is now falsified three times over and must not be re-opened as a disposition question.
frontier.mechanism: Both entries state that target needs a load that is both unshared and early-in-$a1 and that this is the one combination the law excludes at 66 instructions, so closing the function requires a C variable assigned more than once. s14's W5 exhibited it at 66 instructions; s15 bought the $a0 seat the entries called unreachable; s16's K7 exhibits target's complete three-load geometry -- slot, register and count -- at 66 instructions in ordinary C, and L1 holds both register seats at once.
frontier.next_probe: None needed; the correction is banked in evidence.md s16 sections 1-2, hypotheses.md H-s16-1/H-s16-2 and the two new rejected/ headers. The next session should grind the K7 and N2 spines, not the disposition.
